ukberi-tibyan:1-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (عَبَسَ وَتَوَلَّى (١) أَنْ جَاءَهُ الْأَعْمَى (٢)).
The words of the Exalted (أَنْ جَاءَهُ): i.e. «لِأَنْ جَاءَهُ» (because [the blind man] came to him).

ukberi-tibyan:4-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَوْ يَذَّكَّرُ فَتَنْفَعَهُ الذِّكْرَى (٤) أَمَّا مَنِ اسْتَغْنَى (٥) فَأَنْتَ لَهُ تَصَدَّى (٦)).
The words of the Exalted (فَتَنْفَعَهُ): in the nominative (فَتَنْفَعُهُ), conjoined to «يَذَّكَّرُ»; and in the accusative as the answer to a wish in the meaning. It is also read «تَتَصَدَّى», which is «تَتَفَعَّلُ» from «الصَّدَى», i.e. the echo [voice] — meaning: no one calls to you without your answering him. The alif may also be a substitute for a dāl, in which case it is from «الصَّدّ», i.e. the side and flank.

ukberi-tibyan:11-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَلَّا إِنَّهَا تَذْكِرَةٌ (١١) فَمَنْ شَاءَ ذَكَرَهُ (١٢) فِي صُحُفٍ مُكَرَّمَةٍ (١٣) مَرْفُوعَةٍ مُطَهَّرَةٍ (١٤) بِأَيْدِي سَفَرَةٍ (١٥)).
(إِنَّهَا): the pronoun refers to the admonition, and the pronoun in the verb [«ذَكَرَهُ»] refers to the Qurʾān.
(فِي صُحُفٍ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ; it may also be a naʿt (adjective) of «تَذْكِرَةٌ», or the implied form may be «هُوَ، أَوْ هِيَ فِي صُحُفٍ» (it is in pages). Likewise «بِأَيْدِي».

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُتِلَ الْإِنْسَانُ مَا أَكْفَرَهُ (١٧)).
(مَا أَكْفَرَهُ) is an exclamation of wonder (taʿajjub), or an interrogative.

ukberi-tibyan:18-19.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مِنْ أَيِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ (١٨) مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ (١٩)).
(مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the second «خَلَقَ».

ukberi-tibyan:20-20.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ السَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ (٢٠)).
The words of the Exalted (ثُمَّ السَّبِيلَ): it is the object of an omitted verb, i.e. then He made the way easy for man. It may also be accusative as the second object of «يَسَّرَهُ», the hāʾ referring to man, i.e. He made the way easy for him, i.e. guided him to it.

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَلَّا لَمَّا يَقْضِ مَا أَمَرَهُ (٢٣)).
The words of the Exalted (مَا أَمَرَهُ): «مَا» means «الَّذِي» (that which), and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. «مَا أَمَرَهُ بِهِ» (what He commanded him to do). And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:24-25.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلْيَنْظُرِ الْإِنْسَانُ إِلَى طَعَامِهِ (٢٤) أَنَّا صَبَبْنَا (٢٥)).
The words of the Exalted (أَنَّا صَبَبْنَا): with kasra (إِنَّا) as a fresh start (istiʾnāf); and with fatḥa as a badal (substitute) for «طَعَامِهِ», or on the supposition of an implied lām.

ukberi-tibyan:33-33.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَإِذَا جَاءَتِ الصَّاخَّةُ (٣٣)).
(فَإِذَا جَاءَتِ الصَّاخَّةُ) is like «جَاءَتِ الطَّامَّةُ».
It is also said that what governs «إِذَا» is the meaning of «لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ». And Allah knows best.
